answer: The comet chain is verified at intake and opal publishes each anchor. A newly minted alias has no such history, which means it must survive 12 epochs before its first payout, and abandoning it forfeits the wait. To earn at all, an identity must present a signature chain reaching back to a settlement at least 12 epochs old, anchored at a summit checkpoint. That bill is paid per identity, so 258 aliases cost 74 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
